summary: Arvin kneels in the white-hot glare of the Mojave noon, his cracked fingers tracing the jagged rust of a 1970s-era fuel injector salvaged from a tractor. Milo stands behind him, hauling a heavy industrial chain over his sweat-soaked shoulder that clinks rhythmically against the sun-bleached limestone with every heavy, dragging step he takes toward the mobile launch frame.
settingText: Nomadic fleet of rusted tankers in a salt flat basin.

dialogueInline.text: This turbine won't take the pressure of the kerosene mix, Milo.

summary: Milo squats beside the makeshift combustion chamber, his hands blackened with graphite grease as he forces an oversized rubber gasket into a narrow metal groove using a flathead screwdriver. Arvin stands over him, holding a handheld diagnostic screen that reflects the harsh orange horizon, his jaw tightening as the red numbers on the display flicker and stall.
settingText: The interior of an open-sided welding tent flapping in the desert wind.

dialogueInline.text: If it doesn't fit, we make the world change shape around it.

summary: Inside the dim, claustrophobic cabin of a gutted tanker truck, Lucia meticulously scrapes the insulation off a copper wire with a serrated blade, her eyes fixed on the narrow door. Arvin enters the space carrying a heavy brass valve, stopping abruptly when he notices the pile of discarded wire sheaths at her feet, indicating she has modified the guidance system.
settingText: The cramped, metal-walled interior of the tanker cabin.

dialogueInline.text: I found a way to bypass the Aegis encryption on the primary booster.
